1987-716.2.fate: \citet[Theorem 4.1, equations (28)--(33)]{veselovwu2020geodesic} gives the calculation and explicitly attributes it to Knörrer 1982. The original DOI was located \citep{knorrer1982geodesics}, but the original full paper could not be opened.

1987-741.2.fate: \citet[\S1 and the applications]{wantzel1837constructions} treats algebraic constructibility and trisection. The two impossibilities have different proofs; quadrature is not a consequence solely of finite Galois theory. The opened publisher record verifies \citet{lindemann1882pi}; its original proof was not read in this run.

1987-728.4.fate: The order-three characterization predates the seminar: \citet{loewylondon1978inverse} appeared in 1978, with its precise alternatives recorded in \citet[p.~506]{ranteng2024patterns}; the latter treats prescribed order-three zero patterns in 2024. \citet[Theorems~3.9--3.12; Sections~4--5, 8]{johnsonpaparella2025perron}, first circulated in September 2024 and published in 2025, develops geometry and realizing families for joint stochastic spectra. \citet[Section~2]{croninlaffey2018diagonalizable}, preprint January 2017 and publication July 2018, records the five-dimensional obstruction used below. Section~\ref{dev:stochastic} gives complete low-dimensional proofs and an explicit account of what these sources do not solve.
1987-728.4.present_status: As of 11 November 2026: low-dimensional realizations and many structural tests are known, but the checked literature supplies no explicit general characterization in orders at least five. Fixed-order membership for effectively encoded algebraic input is decidable by real quantifier elimination \citep[Chapters~2, 13--14]{basupollackroy2006algorithms}; this does not provide the requested structural description. The chapter proves the two- and three-state cases and exact counterexamples, without claiming novelty or a solution for arbitrary order.

GP-1987-21.status: As of 11 November 2026: partly characterized. The order-three region was known before the talk; recent geometric and prescribed-pattern results do not give a general explicit solution in orders at least five \citep[p.~506]{ranteng2024patterns}\citep[Sections~4--5, 8]{johnsonpaparella2025perron}. Section~\ref{dev:stochastic} supplies complete two- and three-state realizations and proves that even all JLL inequalities are insufficient in order five. Fixed-order algebraic feasibility is decidable, so the unresolved goal is a useful structural characterization with realizing matrices, rather than bare decidability.
